Inspect a mai ALTREP vector

Source: R/altrep.R
mai_vec_info.Rd

With `mai_eval(.altrep = TRUE)` a result stays in mai's output, mapped into memory, and R sees an ALTREP vector over it. `mai_vec_info()` says whether `x` is such a vector and counts what R has asked it for: single elements (`elt`), runs of elements (`region`), the whole data pointer (`dataptr`, which most arithmetic needs) and, on an R built with the proposed `Extract_array_subset` ALTREP method, whole `x[i, j, ...]` requests (`array_subset`).

Usage

mai_vec_info(x)

mai_has_array_subset()

Arguments

x

Any R object.

Value

`NULL` if `x` is not a mai ALTREP vector, otherwise a list with `mapped` (logical) and the counts `elt`, `region`, `dataptr` and `array_subset`. `mai_has_array_subset()` returns `TRUE` when rmai was built against an R that offers `Extract_array_subset`.

Details

Integer results are used in place. Doubles are too, once mai's `NA` values have been rewritten as R's (this happens in memory, on the first full data request). Logical results are converted to R's 4-byte layout on the first full data request.

Examples

if (mai_available()) {
  m <- mai_eval("m * 2.0", m = matrix(runif(12), 3), .altrep = TRUE)
  m[2, 3:4]
  mai_vec_info(m)
}
#> $mapped
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $elt
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $region
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $dataptr
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $array_subset
#> [1] 0
#>
